quote.text: The Net interprets censorship as damage and routes around it.
quote.author: Attributed to John Gilmore; quoted by Philip Elmer-DeWitt, TIME, 6 December 1993

stories.kicker: The Meridian Dispatch · The Gulf, day 201
stories.headline: Riyadh stops waiting for the strait to open, and starts changing ships outside it
stories.dek: Escalation and price moved in opposite directions this week. On Thursday the American president weighed aloud whether to “annihilate” the Iranian regime — and Brent fell anyway, because Saudi crude has begun transferring hull to hull off Oman, and the physical system rebuilt its own bypass in six days.

stories.kicker: The Big Picture · The day after
stories.headline: The Fed hiked into an oil shock, and the bond market said thank you
stories.dek: Wednesday punished everything: a nineteen-year high in the ten-year, a dollar through 100, gold down a hundred and twenty-six dollars in hours.

stories.kicker: Down the Rabbit Hole · Model rocketry
stories.headline: The alphabet is a logarithmic scale, and the law draws its line at one hundred and sixty newton-seconds
stories.dek: Every letter in a rocket-motor code doubles the one before it, so the gap from an A to an M is a factor of about four thousand.

stories.kicker: The Little Red Dot · The air, and the price of a car
stories.headline: The rain bought two days, not a resolution — and on Thursday the particles came back
stories.dek: Yesterday this page recorded the haze easing. The agency’s own daily numbers now show the easing was a dip inside an ongoing episode: fine-particle readings fell to 34–59 micrograms on Tuesday and climbed to 46–78 by Thursday evening, with dry conditions holding and the wind unchanged.

stories.kicker: Buy It Once · Fountain-pen ink & paper
stories.headline: The most celebrated ink in the hobby does not reliably dry — and that is not a defect, it is the mechanism
stories.dek: Ink is barely thicker than water, and two knobs govern everything it does. Learn them and you can judge any bottle and any sheet cold — including why the sheen you are paying for is the same physical fact as the smudge on your cuff.

stories.kicker: Silicon & Sovereignty · A model that will not talk to you
stories.headline: Forty million dollars for a model whose only outputs are yes, no, and a number
stories.dek: TypeSafe AI came out of stealth on Monday with a model called Jev that refuses to write prose, code or conversation.

stories.kicker: Gear We’re Watching · Canon EOS R8 Mark II
stories.headline: Four hundred dollars buys a stabiliser, a joystick and a card slot you can reach — and the same sensor as 2023
stories.dek: Announced on Tuesday with reviews landing inside a day, Canon’s cheapest full-frame body finally has stabilisation in it.

stories.headline: Twelve and a half thousand dollars for one box instead of four — and the trade press says so out loud
stories.dek: McIntosh has folded a preamplifier, a network streamer, a DAC, a phono stage and a headphone amp into a single chassis with the blue meters on the front.

stories.kicker: Culture Desk · Two cyberpunks open today
stories.headline: The best-reviewed video-game adaptation ever recorded opens on the same Friday as a thirty-year-old masterpiece in four K
stories.dek: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil is in theatres and IMAX from today with a Rotten Tomatoes score in the high nineties and no audience score at all. Lionsgate is putting Ghost in the Shell back into eight hundred North American cinemas the same day. One bill, two arguments about what an adaptation owes its source.

stories.kicker: Raising Them Well · The Finnish cohort, read properly
stories.headline: More screen time through childhood, slightly faster thinking at sixteen — and a second finding nobody reported
stories.dek: A Finnish cohort followed 260 children for eight years and found that accumulating more screen time tracked with marginally better cognitive processing.less unsupervised physical activity did the same — which is the half that tells you what the study is probably measuring.

stories.kicker: The Long Game · When the press release oversells the paper
stories.headline: “You need 560 minutes a week” — and an Oxford professor who says that is not what the study found
stories.dek: A large UK Biobank analysis put substantial cardiovascular benefit at three to four times current guidance.

stories.headline: What’s worth booking — sumo on sale tomorrow, a snow hall closing in twelve days, and a correction on BTS
stories.dek: The bookable calendar, Singapore and the region, each item hunted for its own cancellation before it was printed.

stories.headline: The Battle for Solar Energy has a new front, and it runs through your fuse box
stories.dek: In 2016 Colombo launched a campaign with a war poster’s name and persuaded tens of thousands of households to become electricity generators.
